Yes, we were trying to remove **catch-all ownership**, not every broad-sounding directory. The current refactor keeps [client/application](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/README.md:1) as the composition root: it registers shared hosts, assembles commands, starts the app, and connects product chrome to the shell. Account, settings, library, navigation, and other workflows have moved to named owners.

Your concern is still valid. `application` is only justified while it stays limited to that wiring. The current tree has a boundary worth revisiting: several `client/surfaces` files import application’s `paint` and `branding` components, even though application also composes surfaces. So the catch-all has been substantially reduced, but the dependency direction is not fully clean yet. I made no changes.

content.text:
I reviewed the current dirty `dev` checkout read-only. **The main unfinished work is splitting mixed files and correcting ownership edges, not renaming every broad folder.**

| Priority | Leftover | What I would do |
|---|---|---|
| High | [shared/utils/utils.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/shared/utils/utils.ts) | Split it. It mixes product-host parsing, URL validation, version comparison, IDs, and embed sanitization. Put each function with its consumer or a narrowly named shared module, then remove the generic file. Its `generateUID` appears unused; verify before deleting it. |
| High | [client/config](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/config) | Reduce its mixed ownership. Product navigation belongs with product configuration; focus, memory, and clipper event contracts belong with their event or extension owners; metadata belongs with its shell owner; confirmation types belong with notifications. Keep genuinely low-level product identity and action contracts in a neutral owner where lower layers can import them. Don’t wholesale rename `config`. |
| High | [client/application](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/README.md) | Keep composition and startup wiring. Fix the reverse imports: surfaces currently import application’s `ComponentResolver`, loading view, and logo. Supply rendering and branding through the existing hosts or explicit props so application remains the assembly layer. Then remove the unused `@nucleum/application` dependency from `features/package.json`. |
| Medium | [shared-state/resources](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shared-state/resources) | Keep shared selection, recents, panel state, and narrow hosts here. Review [resource.actions.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shared-state/resources/resource.actions.ts) and [bulk-editor.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shared-state/resources/bulk-editor.ts): they combine mutations with context-menu items, icons, and feedback. Move connected action presentation into `features/records`, retaining only genuinely shared state and contracts. |
| Medium | [shell chrome](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shell/topNav/TopNavLeftLogo.svelte) | `TopNavLeftLogo` still calculates subscription status, and [LeftNavOfflineStatus](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shell/leftPanel/LeftNavOfflineStatus.svelte) reads account mode and chooses settings actions. Have the application chrome adapter pass those values and callbacks into shell presentation. |
| Medium | Large files in otherwise correct owners | Split [datafn.store.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/datafn/datafn.store.ts) by lifecycle, storage, status, and E2EE coordination; split [DataSettings.svelte](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/surfaces/settings/DataSettings.svelte) by backup, restore, sync, and encryption controls; split [LibraryRecordsPane.svelte](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/surfaces/library/LibraryRecordsPane.svelte) by query coordination and rendering. Their folders are appropriate; the files carry too many jobs. |
| Lower | Misfiled surface and legacy files | Move [ExtensionLoginStatusPage.svelte](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/surfaces/settings/ExtensionLoginStatusPage.svelte) to account. Reassess the referral [ShareToFriends.svelte](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/surfaces/settings/ShareToFriends.svelte) under sharing. Split [persistence.utils.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/persistence/persistence.utils.ts) so browser storage and device access point identity have named homes. Move [surreal.utils.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/shared/utils/surreal.utils.ts) beside the legacy server sync code that uses it. |

I would **keep** `client/runtime`, `client/shared-state`, `client/shell`, `client/surfaces`, `client/ui/compositions`, and `client/application` as named architectural layers. Their charters give them coherent jobs. `server/common` and `shared/dbo` still serve legacy paths, so they need a separate migration decision rather than an organization-only move.

The best order is: split the generic utility file and mixed config contracts; correct application-to-surface and shell-to-account ownership; then split the large coordinators. Each move should update callers directly, without compatibility re-exports, and run the repository’s architecture/type checks plus checks for the affected products. No files were changed and no checks were run for this read-only assessment.

 `client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively.  The former `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, and `client/events` directories are retired. App context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts have explicit owners under `client/shared-state`. Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. New state follows semantic ownership and must not recreate a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory; `client/shared-state` is the single approved shared-state workspace and keeps named owners with no root barrel.

DataFn resource selection, storage lifecycle, runtime policy and remote transport have named modules; `datafn.store.ts` owns the live client and lifecycle. content.text:
`client/application` still has a purpose in the new design: it is the **composition root**. It starts the running app and connects code owned by the other packages. It should be small, and it should not become the home for anything merely used across the app. That is the distinction the refactor is aiming for in the [application charter](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/README.md:1).

| Owner | The question it answers | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| [Features](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/features/README.md:1) | What content can a user create and manage? | Memory, focus, collections, calendar, record actions. |
| [Surfaces](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/surfaces/README.md:1) | What app-level task or cross-feature screen is the user using? | Account, settings, subscription, search, command bar, library. |
| [Shell](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shell/README.md:1) | Where does content appear, and how does the user navigate to it? | URL navigation, tabs, sidebars, panels, split views, modal chrome. |
| [Application](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/README.md:6) | How are those owners connected and started for this product? | Register hosts, assemble commands, mount startup layers, supply connected chrome. |

The dependency rule makes this concrete: features cannot reach into surfaces or application; shell cannot reach into surfaces, products, or application; application can connect them at the top. For example, a record action belongs to `features/records`, browsing records belongs to `surfaces/library`, its panel and URL behavior belong to `shell`, and registering the renderer that connects them belongs to `application`.

## What remains in `client/application`

There are **19 source files**, in five bounded areas:

| Area | Why it stays |
|---|---|
| [composition](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts:1) | Registers the concrete command, renderer, navigation, shortcut, file, product, and UI hosts. [global-commands.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/composition/global-commands.ts:1) assembles commands defined by their owners. This is the clearest composition-root work. |
| [layers](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/layers/BaseLayer.svelte:1) | `BaseLayer` and `UserBaseLayer` control startup order and mount the resulting app. [AuthGuard](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/layers/AuthGuard.svelte:1) applies the product’s access requirement while delegating session work to account. 1. difference bw application/chrome and shell?
2. should we rename application/ to composition/ ?

**`shell` owns the frame; `application/chrome` fills its connected slots.**

For example, [TopNav](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shell/topNav/TopNav.svelte) owns the nav layout and behavior. [WiredTopNav](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/chrome/WiredTopNav.svelte) supplies the product logo, account picture, search input, and bulk edit bar. Those implementations belong to their own surface or product; application connects them to shell. This keeps shell from importing surfaces or products. If an `application/chrome` file grows into a workflow, that workflow should move to its owner and leave only the connection here.

**I would keep `client/application`, rather than rename it to `client/composition`.** Composition is its main job, but the package also owns startup layers, access gating, connected chrome, branding selection, and action rendering. It already has a `composition/` subfolder, so a top-level rename would either produce `composition/composition` or require another reorganization without improving ownership. The stronger safeguard is the current restricted set of subfolders and the architecture rule against new root workflows. See the [application charter](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/README.md:1).

It has no runtime implementation: - [browser-runtime.d.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/ambient/browser-runtime.d.ts) describes the Chrome extension runtime, storage, tabs, and `window.chrome`. - [third-party.d.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/ambient/third-party.d.ts) describes CryptoJS, Instagram embeds, native configuration on `window`, and types for three external packages. - [youtube.d.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/ambient/youtube.d.ts) describes the YouTube player globals. The app TypeScript configs include these declarations. `ambient` is a reasonable name for this bounded purpose; ordinary app types and workflows should stay with their owners. The [type ownership guide](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/type-ownership.md:7) says the same. **There is no maintained visual dependency map in the architecture docs.** The current references are the prose [client boundaries guide](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:24) and the executable [architecture checker](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/tools/check/architecture.mjs:331). Here is a simplified map; arrows mean “may consume,” not “must import”: ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Apps, routes, extensions"] --> B["Products and composition
product setup and final wiring"] B --> C["Surfaces
account, settings, library, commands"] B --> D["Features
memory, focus, records, etc."] C --> D C --> E["Shell
navigation, panels, overlays"] D --> E C --> F["Shared state
named state and host contracts"] D --> F E --> F F --> G["Runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema"] C --> H["UI
portable presentation"] D --> H E --> H H --> I["Theme and shared utilities"] ``` The key restrictions are: `ui` cannot reach product or domain code; `shared-state` cannot reach features, surfaces, shell, products, or composition; features cannot reach surfaces, products, or composition; shell cannot reach surfaces, products, or composition; surfaces cannot reach composition. `runtime` and `datafn` cannot reach the higher UI and workflow layers. `config`, `static`, and `theme` supply identifiers, assets, and presentation foundations; `next/noop` is a small empty Next-product overlay. `ambient` sits outside the runtime import graph. This is an **ownership overview**, not a complete dependency DAG. Products and surfaces currently reference one another in source, and the checker enforces specific forbidden edges rather than a single exhaustive “may import” matrix. No files were changed.  The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary.
+
+## Client dependency DAG
+
+`tools/check/client-dependency-matrix.json` is the authoritative matrix for direct imports between top-level `client/` owners. An owner may also import its own files. `npm run check:architecture` rejects imports outside the matrix, including type-only imports, and rejects cycles in the allowed matrix itself. Tests and stories are outside this production-source gate. The existing portability and semantic-owner checks still apply within each owner. In particular, `client/ui` is one package in this matrix, with its separate rule that lower UI layers cannot import `compositions`.
+
+```mermaid
+graph LR
+  extensions --> composition
+  routes --> composition
+  composition --> products
+  products --> surfaces
+  surfaces --> features
+  features --> shell
+  shell --> shared_state[shared-state]
+  shared_state --> datafn
+  datafn --> runtime
+  runtime --> persistence
+  persistence --> config
+  config --> next
+  next --> ui
+  ui --> theme
+```
+
+The arrows show one valid ordering, not every permitted direct import. The full direct-import matrix is:
+
+| Importing owner | May import these client owners |
+| --- | --- |
+| `extensions` | `app.css`, `composition`, `config`, `datafn`, `features`, `persistence`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `surfaces`, `ui` |
+| `routes` | `app.css`, `composition`, `config`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `products`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `surfaces`, `ui` |
+| `composition` | `config`, `datafn`, `features`, `persistence`, `products`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `static`, `surfaces`, `ui` |
+| `products` | `config`, `datafn`, `features`, `next`, `runtime`, `shared-state`, `shell`, `surfaces`, `ui` |

+| `runtime` | `persistence` |
+| `persistence` | `config` |
+| `config` | `next` |
+| `next` | `ui` |
+| `ui` | `theme` |
+| `theme`, `static`, `app.css` | no other client owner |
